text: Chapter 2 built a Bicep template provisioning Overlook's Azure SQL environment. Chapter 3 secured it with encryption, masking, auditing, and least-privilege roles. Chapter 4 built and tested a real disaster recovery plan. Chapter 5 automated health checks and alerting. Chapter 6 kept the platform fed with real data. Chapter 7 proved all of it under an unannounced drill and presented the results to the board.

Every one of those chapters traces back to a specific sentence in Lesson 1's board mandate. That's not a coincidence — it's the entire discipline this capstone was built to practice: starting from a real business requirement and building exactly what answers it.

This capstone closes out a three-part arc at Overlook: the Beginner capstone asked does this work at all, the Intermediate capstone asked is this fast, and this Advanced capstone asked is this a platform a board can actually trust with patient data. That's the same arc a real database career follows.

A real platform is never actually finished — hardening the Bicep template further, extending monitoring, and scheduling recurring drills are genuine next steps. And the skills you practiced here — IaC, security design, tested HA/DR, automation, and a real ETL feed, all tied to a business mandate — are exactly what to describe in your next interview, in outcomes and real numbers. Congratulations on finishing this capstone.
